slides.texte_overlay:
habits that make you
the most articulate
man in the room
Think in threes. "There are three reasons..." Structuring your answer in three clear points makes you sound organised, confident and easy to follow.
Use short sentences when it matters. Long, winding sentences lose people. Say the important part in eight words or fewer, then explain the rest.
Replace filler words with pauses. Every "um" and "like" becomes a one-second silence. Pauses sound thoughtful and calm, fillers sound unsure.
Learn to tell one great story. Practise it until it's smooth, with a clear start, middle and end. A man who tells stories well always holds the room.
Feed your vocabulary daily. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and new words and ideas slowly make their way into how I speak.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. New words and ideas slowly make their way into how I speak.

slides.texte_overlay: Match your words to your listener. Simple with kids, precise with experts, warm with friends. Truly articulate men adapt, they don't show off.
End with a clear sentence. "So my answer is yes." Finishing strong tells people you knew exactly where you were going all along, and they remember your point.
